slides.texte_overlay:
How to negotiate a better
price without being pushy
Ask a simple question first. "Is this the best price you can do?" Said calmly, with a smile. You'd be surprised how often the answer is no, followed by a better number.
Know what it costs elsewhere. Two minutes of research before you walk in. "I saw it for a bit less across town, can you get close to that?" Real numbers make a fair request easy.
Be friendly with the person, firm on the number. Ask about their day, thank them for their time. People give better deals to customers they actually like dealing with.
Buy more, ask for more. "If I take both, what can you do?" Bundling gives the seller a reason to move without feeling like they're losing, and you both walk away happy.
Stay curious about how things work. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a calmer, sharper head makes every negotiation feel less stressful.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A calmer, sharper head makes every negotiation feel less stressful, even the awkward ones.

slides.texte_overlay: Be ready to walk away, politely. "Thanks, I'll think about it." Meaning it is your strongest position. Many deals improve the moment you sincerely start heading for the door.
Pay attention to timing. End of the month, end of the day, end of the season. Sellers have targets, and asking at the right moment often gets you a better price without any pushing.
